exposure: 1g IV paracetamol in 100 ML normal saline
outcome: post-cesarean pain (measured by Visual Analogue Scale)
post-cesarean bleeding (assessed by clinical examination, Hemoglobin measurement, and Pad Score)
cohort: The study included 88 patients (15-45 years old, ASA class I and II) who underwent elective cesarean section under spinal anesthesia.
finding: Intravenous paracetamol was significantly more effective than diclofenac suppository in controlling post-cesarean pain and bleeding.
